nodes.label: Block rendering pipeline (Payload Block → Resolver → View Model → Renderer → Section)
nodes.norm_label: block rendering pipeline (payload block → resolver → view model → renderer → section)
nodes.rationale: Separates the CMS schema for a block (manual vs automatic selection) from the rendered UI Section, so a Section never needs to know whether its data came from manual or automatic content selection; unknown blocks log and skip instead of crashing the page.

nodes.label: Tag-based cache and targeted revalidation
nodes.rationale: Using conceptual cache tags (post:{id}, category:{id}, home, navigation, footer, settings) instead of full rebuilds lets publish/update operations invalidate only the dependent content, while Draft Mode must never serve stale public cache to a previewing editor.

nodes.label: Data Access Layer (src/lib/data)
nodes.rationale: Centralizing Payload queries in one layer (getPostBySlug, getLatestPosts, searchPosts, etc.) keeps presentational components query-free and allows the backend to be swapped without touching UI components.

nodes.label: Payload/Next.js separation of responsibilities
nodes.rationale: Payload decides what content exists and its order; Next.js decides how it looks. This split keeps the CMS from emitting arbitrary CSS/HTML/scripts and keeps presentation logic out of the CMS, preventing an uncontrolled visual builder and preserving a consistent editorial design system.

nodes.label: React Server Components by default
nodes.rationale: Minimizes client-side JavaScript and supports progressive enhancement; only components with a genuine browser need (mobile nav, share actions, carousels, accordions) become Client Components.

nodes.label: Source-of-truth conflict priority order
nodes.rationale: Establishes a deterministic precedence (Master Spec > active OpenSpec change > existing verified implementation > tool/skill guidance > agent judgment) so that when instructions conflict, agents resolve deterministically instead of guessing or introducing a third architecture.

nodes.label: ESM Required for Payload CLI Load (ERR_REQUIRE_ASYNC_MODULE fix)
nodes.norm_label: esm required for payload cli load (err_require_async_module fix)

nodes.label: Presentational components do not query Payload directly (rule)
nodes.norm_label: presentational components do not query payload directly (rule)

nodes.label: Project skills routing/precedence policy
nodes.rationale: Loading every installed skill for every task would duplicate guidance, create conflicting heuristics and waste context; routing precedence (Master Spec/OpenSpec > project architecture > most task-specific skill > broad audit skill) keeps only materially relevant skills active.

nodes.label: cms-access-control capability
nodes.rationale: D1: Posts/Pages access.read returns true for authenticated users and restricts anonymous requests to _status:published; Posts additionally declares create/update:isAdminOrWriter and delete:isAdmin after task-16.3 live verification found that Payload defaults any undefined access operation to () => true, which had briefly left Posts create/update/delete open to unauthenticated requests — the other 6 collections already defined their full access block. D2: Users keeps collection-level read open but hides email/role/active via field-level access so the public author shape (displayName/slug/avatar/bio/socialLinks) stays readable without exposing sensitive fields; rejected access.read:()=>false at the collection level. D3: a minimal beforeLogin hook blocks session tokens for active:false accounts, deliberately narrow so it doesn't touch other lifecycle behavior reserved for Phase 3.

nodes.label: environment-validation capability
nodes.rationale: Bootstrap D3: validate critical env vars (DATABASE_URI, PAYLOAD_SECRET) with Zod in a server-only module (src/lib/env/) invoked by both payload.config.ts and Next.js server startup, so a missing/invalid value fails explicitly at boot/build rather than later at runtime; rejected validating only inside route handlers as insufficient. Payload-cms-core D9 later modifies this: Payload's CLI (generate:types, migrate:create) loads payload.config.ts outside the Next.js bundler via a stricter loader that cannot load a module guarded by 'server-only', cannot resolve the tsconfig '@/*' alias, and chokes on richtext-lexical's top-level await. Fix: a second minimal module src/lib/env/payload.ts (no server-only guard, validates only DATABASE_URI/PAYLOAD_SECRET) used exclusively by payload.config.ts, while src/lib/env/index.ts keeps its server-only guard for the rest of the app; rejected removing the server-only guard entirely because it would weaken protection against accidental client-bundle inclusion.

nodes.label: media-collection capability
nodes.rationale: D11: Media.mimeTypes excludes image/svg+xml in this phase because SVG can carry active content and no sanitization mechanism exists yet; deferred to a later phase alongside sanitization.

nodes.label: Layout Primitives (capability)
nodes.rationale: Provides the container primitive and responsive foundations (breakpoints, gutters, readable widths) that future pages/sections will consume, without implementing those pages.

nodes.label: Editorial Components (capability)
nodes.rationale: Provides the presentational, data-free editorial component set as reusable foundation for later-phase pages.

nodes.label: Presentational-only Component Pattern
nodes.rationale: No editorial component may query Payload directly (Local API, REST/GraphQL, or DB); all data arrives via props, keeping components reusable and testable independent of the CMS.

nodes.label: D4: ArticleCard against ArticleCardData contract, not Post
nodes.norm_label: d4: articlecard against articlecarddata contract, not post

nodes.label: Brand/Semantic Color Tokens (brand-red, ink, paper, border, success/warning/error/info)
nodes.norm_label: brand/semantic color tokens (brand-red, ink, paper, border, success/warning/error/info)

nodes.label: Accessibility Foundation (capability)
nodes.rationale: Bakes focus, touch-target, contrast and reduced-motion requirements into Phase 4 primitives/components instead of deferring to a later Phase 11 audit.

nodes.label: Restricted Radius/Shadow Scale
nodes.rationale: Radius limited to 4/8/12/16/999 with cards at 12-16px; shadows reserved for menus/overlays/dropdowns/floating UI so cards avoid a pronounced SaaS-style elevated look, keeping the editorial aesthetic.

nodes.label: Design Tokens (capability)
nodes.rationale: Establishes a single source of visual tokens (color, radius, shadow) in globals.css, replacing shadcn's generic neutral palette and dropping unneeded dark mode for V1.

nodes.label: shadcn Primitives Policy (capability)
nodes.rationale: Defines the policy governing shadcn/ui as the project's primitive layer: what gets installed per change, how it's retheme, and what must not happen (mass install, generic look, a second UI framework).

nodes.label: No Dark Mode in V1
nodes.rationale: Removes the shadcn-generated .dark block, @custom-variant dark, and forbids introducing a theme provider or next-themes, since dark mode is out of scope for V1.

nodes.label: Incremental, Not Mass Installation
nodes.rationale: Forbids `shadcn add --all`; a primitive is added only when a concrete editorial component actually consumes it, avoiding speculative bloat for future phases.

nodes.label: No Inherited Dark Mode in Primitives
nodes.norm_label: no inherited dark mode in primitives
nodes.rationale: Consistent with the absence of dark mode in V1, installed primitives must not expose dark-mode variants or behavior.

nodes.label: Retheming Installed Primitives (no generic shadcn look)
nodes.norm_label: retheming installed primitives (no generic shadcn look)
nodes.rationale: Installed primitives must consume the 60 Segundos Design System tokens (color, radius, typography) instead of keeping shadcn's default neutral oklch appearance.

nodes.label: shadcn/ui as Sole Primitive Base
nodes.rationale: Prevents introducing a competing component library (Material UI, Chakra, Ant Design, Mantine) to avoid fragmenting the UI stack.

nodes.label: Category Theme System (capability)
nodes.rationale: Translates the 10 CMS-stored category theme keys into consumable CSS variables without dynamically interpolated Tailwind classes or arbitrary CMS colors.

nodes.label: Only Controlled Keys, No Arbitrary CMS Color
nodes.norm_label: only controlled keys, no arbitrary cms color
nodes.rationale: An unrecognized theme key must fall back to a Design System default rather than let the CMS drive an arbitrary color, preserving visual consistency and safety.

nodes.label: data-cat-theme Attribute Mapping Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Uses a data-attribute selector instead of runtime Tailwind class interpolation so category colors can't become arbitrary/unsafe and stay statically analyzable.

nodes.label: Explicit Per-theme Contrast Requirement
nodes.rationale: White cannot be assumed as a valid foreground for every theme; light-accent themes (yellow, green, cyan) must define a dark foreground to remain legible.

nodes.label: ArticleCardData Contract (decoupled from Payload Post)
nodes.rationale: ArticleCard is defined against its own frontend data contract instead of Payload's generated Post type, so the data layer must transform CMS data before it reaches the component, keeping presentation decoupled from CMS shape.

nodes.label: No Arbitrary CMS Texture Selection
nodes.rationale: The CMS may only pick from predefined texture variants exposed by the Design System, never an arbitrary URL or value, to keep visual output controlled.

nodes.label: 44px touch target technique (icon ::after 4-way + text min-w-11 + vertical-only ::after)
nodes.norm_label: 44px touch target technique (icon ::after 4-way + text min-w-11 + vertical-only ::after)

nodes.label: Texture Foundation (capability)
nodes.rationale: Exposes paper-grain.webp and newspaper-pattern.webp as reusable, controlled background utilities, without building the Home Hero or other consuming sections.

nodes.label: Typographic Scale (Display XL, H1-H3, Section Heading, Body, Lead, Metadata)
nodes.norm_label: typographic scale (display xl, h1-h3, section heading, body, lead, metadata)

nodes.label: Typography System (capability)
nodes.rationale: Establishes loading/integration of the two type families (Oswald for display, Inter for body/UI) and the scale/usage rules derived from the Master Spec, without implementing full page templates.

nodes.label: D7: Fonts via next/font/google, no font management library
nodes.norm_label: d7: fonts via next/font/google, no font management library

nodes.label: Uppercase Restricted to Nav/Buttons/Section & Category Labels
nodes.norm_label: uppercase restricted to nav/buttons/section & category labels
nodes.rationale: Uppercase must not apply to long article titles or body text, preserving legibility for long-form reading while keeping it as a wayfinding/label device.
